what_its_for: Oxybutynin is used to treat an overactive bladder. It helps reduce the sudden urge to urinate, frequent urination, and accidental leaking of urine (urge incontinence). It works by relaxing the bladder muscles so your bladder can hold more urine.
how_to_take: Take the regular tablets or liquid by mouth with or without food, usually 2 to 3 times a day. If you are taking the extended-release tablet (XL), swallow it whole — do not crush, chew, or break it. Take it at the same time each day. If using the skin patch (Oxytrol), apply it to clean, dry skin on your abdomen, hip, or buttock and change it every 3 to 4 days. If using the gel (Gelnique), apply it to clean, dry skin on your abdomen, upper arms, shoulders, or thighs once daily. Rotate the application site and do not apply to the same spot two days in a row. Wash your hands after applying the gel or patch.
dosing: Doses vary depending on the form prescribed. Common starting doses include: Regular tablet or liquid — 2.5 to 5 mg taken 2 to 3 times daily. Extended-release tablet — 5 to 10 mg once daily; your doctor may increase this up to 30 mg per day based on your response. Skin patch — one patch (3.9 mg/day) applied twice weekly. Gel — one packet (100 mg/gram) applied to the skin once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without asking your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store tablets and liquid at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the liquid tightly closed. For the patch and gel, store at room temperature and keep away from heat and open flame. Keep all forms of this medication out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of used patches carefully by folding them in half with the sticky sides together and throwing them in the trash away from children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking oxybutynin, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing activities that require alertness until you know how this medicine affects you. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, because oxybutynin can reduce sweating and raise your body temperature. Avoid antacids within 1 hour of taking this medication. Do not apply the gel near open flames or smoke until it has fully dried on your skin, as it is flammable. Avoid using other anticholinergic medications without talking to your doctor first, as combining them can increase side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: trouble urinating or no urination at all, severe stomach pain or constipation, eye pain or sudden vision changes, fast or irregular heartbeat, confusion or hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), signs of heat stroke such as hot dry skin, high fever, and not sweating. Also call your doctor if you have a skin rash, difficulty swallowing, or if your symptoms do not improve after a few weeks. Tell your doctor if you have glaucoma, kidney or liver problems, or an enlarged prostate, as these conditions may require extra monitoring.
when_it_works: You may start to notice some improvement in bladder control within the first few days of treatment, but it may take 4 to 6 weeks of regular use to get the full benefit. Be patient and keep taking the medication as directed even if you do not see immediate results. Talk to your doctor if you feel it is not helping after 4 weeks.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with caution. Older adults are more sensitive to side effects like confusion, memory problems, dizziness, and falls. Lower doses are often recommended. The American Geriatrics Society lists oxybutynin as a medication that should be used with extra care in older adults. Children: Oxybutynin can be used in children age 6 and older for bladder control problems, but only under a doctor's direction. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Oxybutynin may pass into breast milk, so ask your doctor before using it while nursing. Kidney or liver problems: Use with caution. Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely.
